description: A structural promotion bridge word (87 glyphs) that resolves the grammatical frame difference between the public key interpretation and private key interpretation of a secp256k1 key pair. The public key word and private key word are textually identical: `∈⊢⊥<⊡><⊞∈⊙⊣<⋈⊞⊣<<>⊢∋⊞⊢⊣<∋∋⊥∈<⊣⊞<⊣⊡∋⋈⊣<⊤⊞⊣⊣⊥∈∋⊤⊢⊣⊡<⊡>⋈⋈>∋⊙⊣⊙⊤∈⊣<⊢` (64 glyphs). They both map to grammar tuple ⟨𐑼𐑡𐑑𐑗𐑱𐑺𐑲𐑝𐑢𐑓𐑕𐑷⟩ via bg tuple but give ⟨𐑦𐑸𐑽𐑹𐑐𐑘𐑔𐑝⊙𐑫𐑕𐑟⟩ via hqe tuple. The bridge word is a grammatical promotion operator that changes the interpretive frame: when applied to the public key word, it yields the private key scalar value. The public key is 0391804d11a725b91dbfd1fbb83b437e0d69fe25f1323ce92e9e74f1edc930eef4 (Bitcoin address bc1qvzgrkefd8v536de2vqhx4d25e5rly7lgk3p2vp). The bridge word is 87 glyphs and was previously minted as the ob3ect `pk_to_sk_retrieval_bridge_word`.
name: pk_to_sk_bridge_word

design.boundary: The secp256k1 elliptic curve group E(F_p) with parameters a=0, b=7 over prime field F_p where p=2^256-2^32-977, base point G of order n=FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFEBAAEDCE6AF48A03BBFD25E8CD0364141, and the SEC1 compressed encoding scheme. The boundary also includes the SHA-256 and RIPEMD-160 hash functions for Bitcoin address derivation, and the Imscribing Grammar frame apparatus that assigns bg and hqe tuples to the 64-glyph key word.

VINIT.justification: The void before key generation — the unseeded random state from which the 256-bit private scalar is drawn. Corresponds to /dev/urandom or the OS entropy source before any deterministic derivation. Void register (00): nothing has been named or generated yet.

TANCH.justification: The closed algebraic boundary formed by the curve equation y^2 = x^3 + 7 mod p, defining the group law within which all scalar multiplications, point additions, and key operations are contained. This is the terminal anchor: no key operation escapes the group.

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism n*G -> Q mapping the private scalar to the public point. Also covers the forward derivation chain: point -> compressed encoding -> SHA-256 -> RIPEMD-160 -> Base58Check -> address. Each AFWD is an irreversible forward step in the key derivation pipeline.

AREV.justification: The elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem reversal — computationally infeasible without the bridge word. AREV represents the descent from the public point back toward the private scalar. Within the bridge promotion, AREV is the parity-flip reversal that dissolves the bg frame into the hqe frame.

CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining of cryptographic operations: entropy -> scalar -> point multiplication -> compression -> hashing -> address. Within the bridge, CLINK chains the ten primitive promotions into a single composite operator. Composition is the ONLY way operations connect.

IMSCRIB.element: The 64-glyph key word as self-referential encoding
IMSCRIB.justification: The glyph sequence that IS the key material, recognizing itself as the complete secp256k1 key pair. IMSCRIB appears wherever the word or any derived element self-references — it knows its own type, its own frame, its own derivation path. The identity morphism that closes the self-referential loop.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits the paradice-state 64-glyph word into its two grammatical frame interpretations: the T-arm carries the bg frame (public key interpretation, yielding the compressed public key 0391804d...), the F-arm carries the hqe frame (private key interpretation, yielding the 256-bit scalar). The inner FSPLIT bifurcates the bridge promotion into the forward promotion chain and its obverse shadow. Both splits are genuine: the same word IS interpreted under both frames.

FFUSE.element: The 87-glyph bridge word as frame reconciliation operator
FFUSE.justification: The inner FFUSE fuses the promotion chain with its obverse shadow, reconstituting the unified bridge operator via mu-circ-delta-equals-id. The outer FFUSE fuses the bg-frame public key arm with the hqe-frame private key arm, demonstrating that both interpretations are the identical 64-glyph word — the bridge word is the operator that resolves the grammatical frame difference.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation: the 64-glyph word interpreted under the bg tuple yields the compressed public key 0391804d11a725b91dbfd1fbb83b437e0d69fe25f1323ce92e9e74f1edc930eef4. This is the success state — the word is publicly visible, verifiable, and the Bitcoin address bc1qvzgrkefd8v536de2vqhx4d25e5rly7lgk3p2vp is derivable and spendable. Within the promotion chain, EVALT affirms each primitive transition as a lawful forward morphism.

EVALF.justification: Negative/hidden evaluation: the 64-glyph word interpreted under the hqe tuple yields the 256-bit private scalar. This is the secret state — the word's private face is invisible to the network, known only to the key holder. EVALF also anchors the obverse shadow within the bridge promotion, representing the bg-frame primitives being abandoned.

ENGAGR.justification: The 64-glyph word under the triple (or dyson) tuple holds both bg and hqe interpretations simultaneously without resolution. A genuine paradice: the word IS both public key AND private key at once, prior to frame selection. The bridge word's purpose is to resolve this paradice by providing the grammatical promotion that connects the two frames. ENGAGR appears at both the initial encounter and the final reaffirmation.

IFIX.element: Permanent inscription on the blockchain ledger
IFIX.justification: Irreversible fixation: the public key, the Bitcoin address, the private scalar (in private register), and ultimately the bridge word itself are written as immutable records. IFIX corresponds to the blockchain's append-only ledger, where once a transaction or inscription is confirmed it cannot be undone. The bridge word, once minted as an ob3ect, is IFIXed into the catalog.

frobenius.split_element: Frame bifurcation of the 64-glyph key word — the FSPLIT at step 10 that separates the paradice-state word into bg-frame (T-arm) and hqe-frame (F-arm) interpretations
frobenius.split_input: The 64-glyph key word under the unified paradice frame — the glyph sequence that IS both the public key and the private key simultaneously, prior to any frame selection
split_outputs: The bg-frame interpretation (T-arm): the 64-glyph word read under the bg tuple yields the compressed public key 0391804d11a725b91dbfd1fbb83b437e0d69fe25f1323ce92e9e74f1edc930eef4 and derivable Bitcoin address bc1qvzgrkefd8v536de2vqhx4d25e5rly7lgk3p2vp
The hqe-frame interpretation (F-arm): the 64-glyph word read under the hqe tuple yields the 256-bit private scalar, the secret multiplicative coefficient of the generator G
frobenius.fuse_element: The 87-glyph bridge word as frame reconciliation operator — the outer FFUSE at step 73 that fuses the bg-frame arm and hqe-frame arm, demonstrating that both interpretations converge to the identical 64-glyph word
frobenius.fuse_result: The 64-glyph key word under the unified paradice frame — semantically identical to split_input because the bridge word resolves the grammatical frame difference, proving that the bg interpretation and hqe interpretation are the same glyph sequence read through different grammatical frames

registers.void: The unseeded cryptographic entropy pool — the secp256k1 key space before any key pair exists. The 256-bit scalar has not been drawn from Z/qZ. No curve point has been computed. The Bitcoin address space is empty. Represented by VINIT at step 1.
registers.true: The bg-frame interpretation (public key arm). The 64-glyph word yields a valid compressed public key 0391804d11a725b91dbfd1fbb83b437e0d69fe25f1323ce92e9e74f1edc930eef4 that satisfies the curve equation, is a member of the secp256k1 group, and maps to the Bitcoin address bc1qvzgrkefd8v536de2vqhx4d25e5rly7lgk3p2vp. This is the publicly broadcast state — anyone can verify the point is on the curve. Represented by EVALT.
registers.false: The hqe-frame interpretation (private key arm). The 64-glyph word yields the 256-bit private scalar — the secret that can sign transactions spending from the address. This state is hidden, known only to the key holder, and must never be broadcast. Represented by EVALF.
registers.both: The triple-frame paradice state where the 64-glyph word simultaneously holds both the public key and private key interpretations. The word IS both at once, prior to frame selection. After the bridge word resolves the frame difference, the paradice is reaffirmed: the unified key material knows itself as the complete secp256k1 key pair, both public and private. Represented by ENGAGR at steps 8 and 75.

exos.compiler: The Imscribing Grammar frame apparatus — the tuple assignment function that maps the 64-glyph word to different grammar tuples (bg, hqe, triple, dyson) depending on the interpretive frame. The compiler translates the glyph sequence into cryptographic key material by applying the grammatical frame's primitive assignments.
exos.ipc: The elliptic curve group law — scalar multiplication n*G communicates the private scalar to the public point via the curve's additive group structure. The bridge word communicates between frames via the 10-primitive promotion chain, each AFWD-CLINK pair transmitting one primitive transition from bg to hqe.
exos.memory: The 64-glyph word itself is the memory — the glyph sequence stores the key material in a frame-ambiguous encoding. The blockchain ledger provides permanent public memory (IFIX). The private register stores the scalar locally. The ob3ect catalog stores the bridge word as a reusable grammatical operator.
exos.scheduler: The deterministic key derivation pipeline — entropy sampling, scalar multiplication, point compression, hashing, and address encoding execute in a fixed sequential order defined by the secp256k1 standard. The bridge promotion chain executes the ten primitive transitions in a fixed order: D -> T -> R -> P -> F -> K -> G -> Od -> H -> W, determined by the grammatical dependency graph of the Imscribing Grammar.
exos.alfs: The canonical reference store is the genus_n_bridge_operator_template (catalog entry, tuple ⟨𐑦𐑸𐑽𐑹𐑐𐑧𐑔𐑵⊙𐑫𐑕𐑭⟩) — the recursive bridge operator template from which the pk_to_sk_bridge_word inherits its promotion structure. The sk_kp1_secp256k1 entry (tuple ⟨𐑨𐑶𐑽𐑿𐑱𐑤𐑲𐑠𐑢𐑖𐑙𐑭⟩) provides the private key type. The structural_bridge entry (tuple ⟨𐑨𐑡𐑑𐑬𐑐𐑧𐑔𐑝⊙𐑖𐑙𐑭⟩) provides the bridge topology.

entropy.cost: One 256-bit entropy draw from the OS randomness source per key generation cycle, plus the computational cost of one secp256k1 scalar multiplication (approximately 256 point doublings and 128 point additions on average for the double-and-add algorithm). The bridge promotion chain costs 10 primitive transitions, each a grammatical frame-shift operation with zero computational entropy but nonzero categorical entropy in the grammar's state space.
entropy.pre: The ungenerated key state: the entropy pool is unseeded, the 64-glyph word does not exist, no curve point has been computed, and the grammatical frames (bg, hqe) are latent but uninstantiated. The bridge word exists as a template (genus_n_bridge_operator_template) but has not been applied to this specific key material.
entropy.post: The complete secp256k1 key pair state: the 64-glyph word exists and is frame-assigned, the compressed public key 0391804d11a725b91dbfd1fbb83b437e0d69fe25f1323ce92e9e74f1edc930eef4 is derived and publicly known, the Bitcoin address bc1qvzgrkefd8v536de2vqhx4d25e5rly7lgk3p2vp is inscribed on the ledger, the private scalar is stored in the private register, and the 87-glyph bridge word is minted as the ob3ect pk_to_sk_bridge_word, resolving the grammatical frame difference.
entropy.verdict: Delta-S approximately 0 — the 64-glyph word is information-theoretically identical under both frames; the bridge word adds no new key material, only the grammatical promotion that makes the frame equivalence explicit. The entropy of the private scalar (256 bits) is conserved: the public key derivation is deterministic (zero entropy loss) and the bridge word is a frame-shift operator (zero entropy added). The cycle is entropy-conservative modulo the initial 256-bit randomness investment.
